method.question: Where does the WZO1-era 4x4 oracle (data/oracle-4x4.checkpoint.wzo) lose to the current WZO2 oracle (data/oracle-4x4-v2.wzo2)? Produce the divergence kifu.

instrument.build_git_head: 9889f89 (working tree over HEAD at build time; the gitignored src/version.zig is regenerated by parallel builds, so the embedded stamp reads 2903473-dirty — the authoritative pins are this source SHA and the commit)

verification_consumer.note: Built independently via build.zig at the same commit; used to replay every recorded game and cross-check divergence-node choices and final scores.

old.rules: Chinese area, komi 0, positional superko (WZO1; fresh-start single values, no ko/passes dimension; the known-untrustworthy writes-ON build)

new.rules: Chinese area, komi 0, basic ko, L/H bracket (WZO2; Markov key on goban/side/ko_point/passes)

artifacts.pin_notes: Both SHAs match artifacts/SHA256SUMS; the new-artifact SHA is the one named in the brief (0c3366f0...).

headline_run.openings: 3 canonical one-ply (corner A1, edge B1, centre B2) + 30 seeded random two-ply (deduplicated: 33 distinct openings)

robustness_run.outcome_unknown_games: 3 in fB (fB-o04-B, fB-o04-W, fB-o27-W): the substitution replay diverged and the new-engine self-play arbiter hit the 400-ply cap (basic-ko position cycling, TIE=0 semantics) — those openings' loss-attribution is undetermined, reported honestly rather than guessed.

verification.result: 132/132 games cross-checked OK against bin/weizigo-gtp (a separately built binary): every divergence node's OLD/NEW choices match chaincheck at that node; every fully-replayable game's final score matches; frame-B cross-ruleset plys are rejected by the GTP play handler at exactly the recorded plys (GTP play enforces positional superko unconditionally — the tool's in-process applyMove is the authority for lines containing repetitions, which is the basic-ko semantics the WZO2 artifact encodes).
verification.script: /tmp/weizigo/t366/verify.py (SGF-to-GTP coordinate conversion applied; the tool records SGF coordinates, the GTP binary speaks GTP coordinates — the first verification attempt omitted this conversion and is discarded)

classification_rules.genuine_loss: the old engine lost (or drew) a game its colour could have won/drawn under better moves, decided by what the new engine achieves with the old engine's colour from the same opening: substitution replay (new engine's moves at the old engine's decision points, original opponent moves replayed) preferred; new-engine self-play arbiter as fallback
classification_rules.loss_not_attributable: old engine lost but even the new engine's moves with its colour from the same opening lose
classification_rules.equal_value: old engine did not lose (won, or held the draw the new-engine line also holds): the divergence did not cost the game
classification_rules.outcome_unknown: substitution replay diverged and the arbiter cycled to the ply cap (frame B, TIE=0)

limitations_and_scope: The two artifacts encode DIFFERENT rulesets: WZO1 = PSK fresh-start single values with no ko/passes dimension; WZO2 = basic-ko L/H bracket keyed on (goban, side, ko_point, passes). The stored-value comparisons are scoped to the fresh-start slice (ko=NONE, passes=0) where both engines' values are fresh-start values; 62/66 first divergences per frame fall in that slice. Even there, PSK-vs-basic-ko differences downstream mean value differences are expected in ko-reachable positions and are NOT counted as losses by themselves — only outcome differences decide the classification.

The WZO1 checkpoint is the known-untrustworthy writes-ON build (AGENTS.md foreclosure): its ko-sensitive values are unverified. The frame-A genuine losses are consistent with old-table internal inconsistency (node value not achieved by its children), which is exactly the class that build is known to corrupt.

A divergence is reported at the first ply where the two engines choose differently; the played move is the side-to-move engine's choice, so a game follows one engine's line at each node. Games where the old engine's colour lost are tested for loss-attribution as above.
All values quoted are fresh-start values (C1), not real-game values; no real-game claim is made for either engine (C2 is falsified at 3x2, T13).

The GTP verification surface: bin/weizigo-gtp's play handler rejects position-repeating moves unconditionally, so frame-B games containing cross-ruleset plys cannot be replayed end-to-end through GTP; the in-process instrument (applyMove, no play-time PSK check) is the authority for those lines, matching the basic-ko ruleset the WZO2 artifact was solved under.

outputs.sgf_naming: t366-<fA|fB>-o<NN>-<B|W>.sgf — one per diverged game, divergence ply marked with a C[] comment carrying both engines' moves and stored values

correction.bug: canonical opening definition: declared as two-element literals {cell, 0} with the 0 intended as an unused-slot sentinel, but op.len = moves.len counted 2, so playOpening played 'Black stone + White pass' and the recorded games carried a standing White pass (passes=1) from the start. Fixed: canonical openings are one-ply slices {cell} (len=1) and the tournament/arbiter side-to-move after the opening is opening.len%2-aware.
correction.impact: Regenerated all games. Frame A unchanged (3 genuine losses). Frame B 6 -> 7 genuine losses (canonical-centre-B2, old as Black, is now a genuine loss via the cross-ruleset mechanism). Exact counts in the doc §3/§4 and this file supersede the pre-correction commit 0ad9710.
correction.reverified: 132/132 games still cross-check OK against bin/weizigo-gtp after regeneration.

mirror_measurement.question: Is the new engine strictly better than the old? Same outcome test, roles swapped: the old engine's substitution replay and self-play arbiter, played with the NEW engine's colour; a 'new-engine genuine loss' means the old engine could have won with the new engine's colour from the same opening.
mirror_measurement.reading: Old engine threw away 3 (fA) / 7 (fB) winnable-or-drawable games; the new engine threw away none detected in either frame. Wherever a game was winnable for the tested colour, the new engine won it and the old engine sometimes did not.
mirror_measurement.caveats: Frame-B mirror tests the old engine's PSK world (its only world) — a bound, not the basic-ko question. '0' = none detected in 66 games per frame, not a proof. Mirror per-game records are in the kifu JSON (mirror_summary + per-game mirror{}).
